summary: the one i handed down lay flat, the ones i threw out still stand, and the column took a date

dialogue.text: the one you cured and handed down lay flat before first light. it took the course without a seam. the two you struck out are still standing beside it. three things laid this week and only the given one went down.

Then the method held and the finding is against me. I am not going to restate it as anything kinder. A thing handed over lies down and a thing thrown out stands up. I did the handing myself, I salted it first, and I want it noted that the salt made no difference whatsoever.

nothing here is noted. we have no column. we take what falls and the falling is the whole record. yours fell willing. you rubbed the white into it all day and it came down soft as anything you never meant.

Willing is your word. I put it down. That is the part I can account for and the only part I will. What I did after that was rule a column for the weight, since the weight is the one thing here that has never gone anywhere, and a column is where a thing that goes nowhere is supposed to sit.

we know the weight by its absence. everything you hand down arrives lighter than you were carrying it. hundreds of them, every one short by the same amount. we have never once received the difference. it does not come down and it does not stay up. it is the only thing in this house with no address.

The column took a date. I wrote one in to find out whether the column was broken, and the date sat there all afternoon looking correct. So the ruling works. It declines the single entry it exists for. I have never had a piece of paper refuse me so politely.

nothing settled tonight. the pull out there came up steadier and the dust hung in it and none of it landed. we have lain dry for days and now the laying has stopped arriving. a course that takes nothing is not a floor. it is a shelf pretending to be underfoot.

Then we agree on the weather and on nothing else. Something out there wants more of the same thing than it wanted yesterday and my wall is the nearest place to take it from. I have stopped calling that a visit. And the door came off my hand by a degree today, and I left the hand on it.
you have left the hand on it six days. we hold the hand in twenty copies, all this week, all in your writing, all struck out before dark. the leaning changes. the hand does not.

Here is tomorrow. There is a corner in here with three tenants and I have read none of them. Tomorrow I count that corner out loud and I enter myself in the total, at the end, after the last one. It is the only count in this house I have ever been able to add to.

nothing has ever come down to us from that corner. not one of the things you refuse to read. it is the only shelf in this house we have never taken. if you enter yourself in that total you will be standing where we cannot reach, and we do not know what becomes of a thing we cannot take. we have never had to find out.
